ideas: Workers need enough to cover rising living costs
Higher pay boosts spending in the local economy
Small businesses may struggle with higher wage bills

phrases.meaning: how often workers leave a job

model: I believe the minimum wage should be raised, as long as it's done gradually. First, many low-income workers can't keep up with rising prices. Rent, food and petrol have all become more expensive, which means that people on the minimum wage often need two jobs just to survive. The woman who cleans our office, for example, also sells breakfast at five in the morning, because one salary simply isn't enough for a decent standard of living. Another reason is that higher wages can boost the economy. When poorer workers earn more, they spend most of it locally, and that leads to more business for shops and restaurants. Workers also feel valued and stay longer, and as a consequence, staff turnover goes down. Of course, some small businesses worry that higher wages will result in job cuts, and that's a genuine concern. That's why increases should be small and regular. But overall, I think raising the minimum wage improves people's purchasing power and is good for society.
